title: Count Elements With Strictly Smaller and Greater Elements
statement: You are given an integer array `nums`. Count the positions `i` for which `nums` holds some value less than `nums[i]` and also some value larger than `nums[i]` (both comparisons are strict). Equal values at different positions are counted separately. Return that count.
notes:
## Intuition

A value has something strictly smaller in the array exactly when it is not the minimum, and something strictly larger exactly when it is not the maximum. So the question reduces to: how many elements are neither the minimum nor the maximum? The brute force would scan the whole array for each element, which is O(n²); knowing just the two extremes answers every element at once.

## Approach

1. Find `smallest` and `largest` in `nums`.
2. Walk through every `value` and count it when `smallest < value < largest`.
3. Return `count`.

When all values are equal, `smallest === largest`, so no value passes the strict test and the answer is `0` without any special case.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [11, 7, 2, 15]`: `smallest = 2`, `largest = 15`. `11` lies strictly between, so `count = 1`; `7` too, so `count = 2`; `2` is the minimum and `15` the maximum, so they are skipped. The answer is `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass for each extreme and one counting pass.
- Space: O(1): three numbers.

## Pitfalls

- The formula `n - count(min) - count(max)` goes negative when every value is the same, because the minimum and maximum are the same elements counted twice; the strict comparison avoids that.
- Use strict `>` and `<`: a copy of the minimum is not smaller than the minimum.
- Duplicates in the middle each count, as in example 2.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `smallest` | minimum of `nums` |
| `largest` | maximum of `nums` |
| `value` | the element being checked |
| `count` | elements found strictly between the extremes |

narration.2: The minimum: any value above it has a strictly smaller element.
narration.3: The maximum: any value below it has a strictly greater element.
narration.4: No element has been counted yet.
narration.6: Check every element of the array once.
narration.7: It needs to be strictly above the minimum and strictly below the maximum.
narration.11: Return how many elements sit strictly between the two extremes.
